title: Equal vision and the peace of the free

verses.sa: नादत्ते कस्यचित्पापं न चैव सुकृतं विभुः । अज्ञानेनावृतं ज्ञानं तेन मुह्यन्ति जन्तवः ॥
verses.tr: The all-pervading one takes neither anyone's wrongdoing nor anyone's good deed. Knowledge is covered by ignorance, and that is why living beings are deluded.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Arjuna feels crushed by the weight of his own actions on the battlefield. What is the divine's true role in all of this? Listen to how Krishna answers.

body.text: The all-pervading one takes neither anyone's wrongdoing nor anyone's good deed. Knowledge is covered by ignorance, and that is why living beings are deluded. Notice the word jantavah, living beings. It places the blame for confusion not on the divine taking away their deeds, but on their own limited state of being. Krishna then shows how destroying that ignorance through knowledge reveals the supreme truth.

verses.sa: ज्ञानेन तु तदज्ञानं येषां नाशितमात्मनः । तेषामादित्यवज्ज्ञानं प्रकाशयति तत्परम् ॥
verses.tr: But for those whose ignorance has been destroyed by knowledge of the true self, that knowledge reveals the supreme reality like the sun.
verses.angle: Adityavat: like the sun, knowledge reveals
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna is describing what happens when a person truly understands. Listen for the image he uses to show this.

body.text: But for those whose ignorance has been destroyed by knowledge of the true self, that knowledge reveals the supreme reality like the sun. The word is Adityavat, like the sun. Just as sunlight instantly removes darkness without effort, knowledge of the Atman reveals the supreme reality the moment ignorance is gone. Krishna now says that those who are fully devoted to that reality reach a state of no return.

verses.tr: Those whose intellect is fixed in That, whose mind is That, who are established in That, and who are devoted to That, go to the state of no return, their impurities washed away by knowledge.
verses.angle: The word tad, That, repeated four times
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna is drawing a line between knowing the truth and living it. Listen for the single word that returns four times, binding the mind and intellect together.

body.text: Those whose intellect is fixed in That, whose mind is That, who are established in That, and who are devoted to That, go to the state of no return, their impurities washed away by knowledge. That single word is tad, That, and it appears four times in this verse. It binds the intellect, the mind, the footing, and the devotion into one single focus on the supreme. Krishna then broadens this vision to show how the wise see that same reality in every living being.

verses.sa: विद्याविनयसंपन्ने ब्राह्मणे गवि हस्तिनि । शुनि चैव श्वपाके च पण्डिताः समदर्शिनः ॥
verses.tr: The wise see the same reality in a learned, humble brahmin, a cow, an elephant, a dog, and an outcaste.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just described a mind fixed in the supreme reality. Now he shows what that mind looks like in practice, as it looks past every social label.

body.text: The wise see the same reality in a learned, humble brahmin, a cow, an elephant, a dog, and an outcaste. Listen to the word samadarshinah, equal-seeing. The wise do not rank beings. They see the same single reality in a learned brahmin and in an outcaste, in a dog and in an elephant. Krishna explains that those who rest in this sameness conquer rebirth here itself, because the supreme reality is flawless and equal.

verses.sa: इहैव तैर्जितः सर्गो येषां साम्ये स्थितं मनः । निर्दोषं हि समं ब्रह्म तस्माद्ब्रह्मणि ते स्थिताः ॥
verses.tr: Those whose mind rests in sameness conquer rebirth here itself. The supreme reality is flawless and equal, so they are established in it.
verses.angle: इहैव, here itself, the conquest is won now
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna now draws the line between seeing sameness and living it. Listen for the exact moment of conquest.

body.text: Those whose mind rests in sameness conquer rebirth here itself. The supreme reality is flawless and equal, so they are established in it. Those whose minds rest in sameness have conquered rebirth here, Krishna says, because Brahman itself is flawless and even. The next verse describes the person who does not rejoice at the pleasant nor shrink from the unpleasant.

verses.sa: न प्रहृष्येत्प्रियं प्राप्य नोद्विजेत्प्राप्य चाप्रियम् । स्थिरबुद्धिरसम्मूढो ब्रह्मविद्ब्रह्मणि स्थितः ॥
verses.tr: One who does not rejoice at the pleasant, and does not shrink from the unpleasant, is steady in understanding, free from delusion, and established in the supreme reality.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: After explaining how the supreme reality is flawless, Krishna now tells what it looks like inside a person. Listen for the mark of a steady mind.

body.text: One who does not rejoice at the pleasant, and does not shrink from the unpleasant, is steady in understanding, free from delusion, and established in the supreme reality. Krishna gives a direct test for a steady mind: the person does not rejoice at the pleasant, and does not shrink from the unpleasant, and this freedom from delusion is what establishes them in the supreme reality. Krishna now asks what happens when a person finds joy inside the true self instead of in outer contacts.

verses.sa: बाह्यस्पर्शेष्वसक्तात्मा विन्दत्यात्मनि यत्सुखम् । स ब्रह्मयोगयुक्तात्मा सुखमक्षयमश्नुते ॥
verses.tr: One who is not attached to outer contacts finds the joy within the true self. Unified with the supreme reality, that person enjoys unending happiness.
verses.angle: Akshayam: happiness that never runs out
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna shows Arjuna how to step out of the restless chase of outer pleasures and find a joy that never fades.

body.text: One who is not attached to outer contacts finds the joy within the true self. Unified with the supreme reality, that person enjoys unending happiness. The word akshayam means imperishable, and it points to a happiness that does not run out. The verse says this joy is found not in the world outside, but within the true self. Next, Krishna turns to the senses themselves and shows that the pleasures they offer are only sources of suffering.

verses.sa: ये हि संस्पर्शजा भोगा दुःखयोनय एव ते । आद्यन्तवन्तः कौन्तेय न तेषु रमते बुधः ॥
verses.tr: The pleasures born from contact with the senses are only sources of suffering. They have a beginning and an end, O Arjuna, and the wise do not delight in them.
verses.angle: Duhkha yoni: a womb of suffering
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna points to one specific word to show what sense pleasures really are. Listen for how he names the suffering hidden inside them.

body.text: The pleasures born from contact with the senses are only sources of suffering. They have a beginning and an end, O Arjuna, and the wise do not delight in them. Listen to one word, duhkha yoni. It means a womb or source of suffering, and Krishna uses it to say that every pleasure born of the senses is merely a source of pain. The wise do not delight in these pleasures. Krishna now turns to the next obstacle, desire and anger, and how to withstand them.

verses.sa: शक्नोतीहैव यः सोढुं प्राक्शरीरविमोक्षणात् । कामक्रोधोद्भवं वेगं स युक्तः स सुखी नरः ॥
verses.tr: Whoever can withstand the surge of desire and anger here before the body falls, is a disciplined person and is truly happy.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna asks Arjuna to look inward, to the rush of desire and anger that arises inside a person before the body falls.

body.text: Whoever can withstand the surge of desire and anger here before the body falls, is a disciplined person and is truly happy. Whoever can bear the surge of desire and anger before the body falls is a yogi and happy. The next verse describes the person who finds happiness within and reaches the supreme reality.

verses.sa: योऽन्तःसुखोऽन्तरारामस्तथान्तर्ज्योतिरेव यः । स योगी ब्रह्मनिर्वाणं ब्रह्मभूतोऽधिगच्छति ॥
verses.tr: One who finds happiness within, delights within, and has inner light alone, becomes one with the supreme reality and reaches freedom in the supreme reality.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: After explaining how to master desire and anger, Krishna now names the person who has already won. Listen for the three inner qualities that mark such a yogi.

body.text: One who finds happiness within, delights within, and has inner light alone, becomes one with the supreme reality and reaches freedom in the supreme reality. The verse names three inner sources. The yogi finds happiness within, delight within, and light within. This marks a person who needs nothing from the outside world. Krishna then tells us that sages who are pure and devoted to the welfare of all beings also attain this same freedom.

verses.sa: लभन्ते ब्रह्मनिर्वाणमृषयः क्षीणकल्मषाः । छिन्नद्वैधा यतात्मानः सर्वभूतहिते रताः ॥
verses.tr: Sages who are free of impurity, free of doubt, self-controlled, and devoted to the welfare of all beings attain freedom in the supreme reality.
verses.angle: Yatatmanah: the pivot between inner peace and outer care
verses.speaker: Krishna

body.text: Sages who are free of impurity, free of doubt, self-controlled, and devoted to the welfare of all beings attain freedom in the supreme reality. Rishis free of stain and doubt, self-controlled and devoted to the welfare of every being, reach nirvana in Brahman. Krishna then says that for those who are free from desire and anger, freedom in Brahman is near on both sides.

verses.sa: कामक्रोधवियुक्तानां यतीनां यतचेतसाम् । अभितो ब्रह्मनिर्वाणं वर्तते विदितात्मनाम् ॥
verses.tr: For those free from desire and anger, with disciplined minds and self-knowledge, freedom in the supreme reality is near on both sides.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna describes a mind at peace with itself, free from craving and rage. Listen for the two states this freedom covers.

body.text: For those free from desire and anger, with disciplined minds and self-knowledge, freedom in the supreme reality is near on both sides. The word abhitah, on both sides, means this peace is immediate, whether the body still lives or has already fallen away. Krishna then gives the exact physical posture and breath control used by such a seeker.

verses.sa: स्पर्शान्कृत्वा बहिर्बाह्यांश्चक्षुश्चैवान्तरे भ्रुवोः । प्राणापानौ समौ कृत्वा नासाभ्यन्तरचारिणौ ॥
verses.tr: Leaving outer objects outside, fixing the gaze between the eyebrows, and balancing the inward and outward breaths moving through the nose.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna shifts from describing the liberated state to giving a practical method. Listen for the way he pairs the inward and outward breaths.

body.text: Leaving outer objects outside, fixing the gaze between the eyebrows, and balancing the inward and outward breaths moving through the nose. Krishna balances the inward and outward breaths, the prana and apana, making them equal as they move within the nose. This equalizing of the breath is the physical anchor that steadies the mind. With the breath balanced, Krishna describes the person who is forever free, having mastered the senses, mind, and intellect.

verses.sa: यतेन्द्रियमनोबुद्धिर्मुनिर्मोक्षपरायणः । विगतेच्छाभयक्रोधो यः सदा मुक्त एव सः ॥
verses.tr: One who has controlled the senses, mind, and intellect, who seeks freedom as the highest aim, and who is free from desire, fear, and anger is forever free.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just described how a sage sits with senses and breath held. Now he states the result of that discipline.

body.text: One who has controlled the senses, mind, and intellect, who seeks freedom as the highest aim, and who is free from desire, fear, and anger is forever free. The sage is not waiting for death to be free. He is already free, because his senses, mind, and intellect are fully mastered. Krishna now says that the person who knows him as the enjoyer of all sacrifice and austerity attains peace.

verses.sa: भोक्तारं यज्ञतपसां सर्वलोकमहेश्वरम् । सुहृदं सर्वभूतानां ज्ञात्वा मां शान्तिमृच्छति ॥
verses.tr: Knowing me as the enjoyer of all sacrifice and austerity, the great lord of all worlds, and the friend of all beings, one attains peace.
verses.angle: maheshvaram, great lord of all worlds
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna's final reassurance on Kurukshetra tells Arjuna that peace arrives from knowing the true nature of the one receiving all offerings, and the next verse begins to describe the yogi.

body.text: Knowing me as the enjoyer of all sacrifice and austerity, the great lord of all worlds, and the friend of all beings, one attains peace. The word maheshvaram, great lord of all worlds, names the supreme ruler of the universe; knowing this ruler as one's own friend brings a peace that needs no further proof. Krishna now defines the true yogi as one who acts without clinging to the fruit of action.

prev.title: Renunciation and action arrive at the same place
